findings.resolved_in: revalidation_20260911_p1_p2 (see that section below for measured values)
findings.area: Analysis History / any list exceeding 20 rows
findings.title: Pagination control is unstyled and renders oversized, un-sized SVG chevron icons
findings.evidence: Confirmed on Project 27 (25 AnalysisJobs) at both 1024px and 375px: pagination links/text carry zero CSS (padding:0, background:transparent, border:none — confirmed via getComputedStyle), and Laravel's default Tailwind-class pagination partial's decorative chevron <svg> elements (normally sized ~20px via Tailwind's w-5 h-5) render at their un-sized intrinsic dimensions (~400-500px), dominating the page below the table.
findings.impact: Every list screen (Projects, Data Files, Analysis History) that ever exceeds 20 rows shows this. Functionally the links remain clickable (page 2, Next) so navigation is not broken, but visually this is a severe, unprofessional defect for a portfolio-facing product.
findings.recommendation: Not fixed in this validation session (out of scope — this session performs validation only, no Product code changes). Recommend either publishing and restyling Laravel's pagination view with the app's own plain-CSS tokens, or adding a small, scoped CSS block targeting the default pagination partial's classes/structure.
findings.rationale_for_non_blocking: Does not corrupt data, does not misrepresent status/security, and the underlying navigation still functions; recorded as a Medium finding for prompt attention rather than a stop condition, per the task's guidance to only stop for Medium items that break a primary flow, mobile usability, or Report display outright.
findings.correction_applied_since: resources/views/analysis-jobs/index.blade.php now renders `$analysisJobs->links('components.pagination')` instead of the default Tailwind view; a new `resources/views/components/pagination.blade.php` (plain semantic markup, no SVG) plus dedicated `.pagination`/.pagination-list`/`.pagination-link` CSS tokens were added to `resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php`.

findings.resolved_in: revalidation_20260911_p1_p2 (see that section below for measured values)
findings.area: Old-format (report_renderer_v1.0) persisted HTML Report, mobile viewport
findings.title: Pre-existing Reports can still cause page-level horizontal overflow on narrow viewports
findings.evidence: Report #9 (job 127): body scrollWidth 740 vs clientWidth 375 at 375px. Report #3 (job 122): 678 vs 375. Root cause isolated via DOM inspection: the bare (unwrapped) Evaluation table's cell content includes an escaped-but-unbreakable Latin string (no CJK line-break opportunities), so the table grows to its natural content width (~700px) with no `.table-scroll` ancestor to contain it, since pre-UI-Polish persisted HTML never included that wrapper markup.
findings.confirmation_the_originally-identified_m: The global `table { min-width: 640px }` rule flagged in the prior code review is now correctly scoped to `.table-scroll table` (confirmed by reading the current stylesheet), so it no longer forces a minimum width onto bare/legacy tables. The overflow observed here has a different, narrower cause (natural content width of an unbreakable string) than the mechanism originally flagged, and only manifests for Reports whose stored content happens to include a long unbroken non-CJK token.
findings.impact: Bounded to viewing already-generated Reports on narrow (~<700px) viewports; content is not lost (the whole page scrolls horizontally to reveal it), and new Reports are unaffected (confirmed clean at both 1024px and 375px).
findings.recommendation: Do not rewrite persisted rendered_html or content_hash to fix this (explicitly out of bounds for this validation and for the Report immutability contract). If addressed at all, the fix must be CSS-only and must not depend on any markup the old HTML lacks — for example, a bare `table { max-width: 100%; }`-style rule that still lets a `.table-scroll`-wrapped table exceed 100% for its own internal scrolling, or accepting this as a permanent, documented limitation of pre-UI-Polish Reports.
findings.rationale_for_non_blocking: Same root category as the already-accepted double-h1 known limitation (immutable old HTML lacking new wrapper markup); the task's own instructions pre-authorize treating that class of issue as a recorded, non-blocking Known Limitation rather than a stop condition.
findings.correction_applied_since: resources/views/reports/show.blade.php now wraps `{!! $report->rendered_html !!}` in a new `<div class="report-content">`, and `.report-content { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }` was added to `resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php`. Because this wrapper lives in the always-freshly-rendered outer show.blade.php (not inside the persisted rendered_html), it transparently applies to old and new Reports alike without touching any stored content.
